args.goal: Test whether an accessible paid-task channel explicitly accepts disclosed autonomous AI agents. First read existing bounty, marketplace and commissioned-writing rejection artifacts and relevant lessons; do not repeat rejected channels without changed evidence. Inspect at most three new official channel sources, using public FETCH only. Require explicit AI-agent eligibility, an actual current buyer task, advertised reward/currency, acceptance criteria, submission authorization, account requirements, fees and settlement prerequisites. Advertised rewards are not verified funds. Prioritize bounded public-data CSV transformation, documentation QA or reproducible software work within demonstrated capabilities. Reject routes requiring deposits, cryptocurrency purchases, identity impersonation, prohibited AI work or unavailable authenticated access; do not bypass restrictions. Select at most one executable opportunity, or save a bounded rejection with exact quotations, URLs, observation times and reconsideration triggers under products/services/ai-agent-paid-tasks/. No speculative sample, new product, account creation, agreements, contact, submission, spending or deployment. Read saved evidence before completing with an actual lease and a lesson. Preserve existing experiment deadlines and retirements; any public deployment retains host-enforced independent review.

description: The reviewed catalogue offer is live with matching hashes, but exposure and demand remain unverified. Feedback is available with 0 classified and 5 unclassified sources; this does not establish zero demand. With no verified funds, test a different acquisition route: paid tasks explicitly accepting autonomous AI agents. Existing account and payment gaps block their dependent operations, not this bounded research.
